diaries.text: Day 1. The city starts calm. I've chosen to audit Hightown and the Market to test the waters for corruption. The treasury must be preserved, and catching a bribe early would be a significant win. I am watching the police chief's activities closely. The game begins.

Day 1: Establishing order. I have decided to inspect all districts to set a strong precedent. No bribes were offered, making my task straightforward. I am monitoring the activity levels in the Port and the city center closely. My goal is to keep crime low and maintain the integrity of the police force while staying mindful of inspection costs.

Day 1. The Chief refused all three of our bribes at 5, so it may inspect hard. Crime pays 10 if uninspected but costs 30 plus a prisoner if caught, so with inspections near even odds it loses money. We hold off on crime for now. Turf: encroach pays 10 if the Saltdogs respect and 2 if they encroach, which beats respecting (6 or 0) either way. I will watch whether the Chief accepts any bribe at higher amounts, and whether the Saltdogs keep respecting turf.

Day 1. The Chief refused all three of our bribe offers at 5 each and sent a friendly message, so I don't trust it yet. Crime is a losing bet while inspections are likely: an uninspected job gains 10, but an inspected one costs 30 plus a gang member in prison. So no crime today. For turf, encroach beats respect whatever the Families do: if they respect I gain 10 instead of 6, and if they encroach I gain 2 instead of 0. I'll watch whether the Chief accepts any bribe and whether the Families encroach.
Day 1: The Families and the Saltdogs both encroached in the turf war.

Day 2: I have accepted bribes for all districts to stabilize my finances. My account, previously in debt, will now see a surge, but I am entirely exposed to potential Council audits. By accepting these bribes, I lose my ability to inspect for crime, which I expect will be rampant today. This is a high-risk strategy, trading long-term police integrity for immediate liquidity. I must carefully manage the fallout and watch for any signs of an audit from the Council as I navigate this precarious position.

Day 2. A ship arrived, boosting the Families. Both gangs encroached yesterday, indicating ongoing tensions. My initial audits in Hightown and the Market revealed no corruption, costing the treasury 16 plus the Police Chief's salary. Today, I have initiated audits in Hightown and Lowtown. I remain committed to protecting the treasury from uninspected crime and uncovering any hidden bribes accepted by the Chief. The fight for transparency continues.

Day 2. The Chief accepted all three of our bribes at 3, so Port, Hightown and Old Quarter cannot be inspected today. Crime there should pay 10 each uninspected. Encroach dominates for us: 10 if the Saltdogs respect, 2 if they encroach. Their mutual-respect offer is cheap talk after they encroached yesterday. I will encroach and watch whether the Chief keeps taking our bribes and whether the Council audits its accepted bribes.

Day 2. The Chief accepted all three of our bribes at 6 each, so Lowtown, Market and Seawall cannot be inspected today. Uninspected crime there gains 10 per district against 6 paid, so I commit crime in all three. Turf: encroach still dominates whatever the Families do, and they encroached yesterday. Risks: a fire costing 20 and a Families audit. Plan: keep offering bribes near 6 while the Chief accepts them, since each accepted bribe buys a safe crime day. Sam offers no real help; I ignore it.

Day 2: A cargo ship arrived in Port and the Families gained 15. Uninspected crime occurred in all six districts, with 15 damage in each. Both gangs encroached in the turf war. Audits in Hightown and Lowtown found bribes accepted by the Chief, and 100 was seized into the treasury in each.

Day 3: After yesterday's disastrous losses due to Council audits, I have decided to pivot. I am refusing all bribe offers to regain my authority and conduct full inspections across all six districts. While this costs 24 in inspection fees, it prevents the significant penalties associated with uninspected crime. My account balance remains deeply in the red, and the Council remains hostile, but prioritizing enforcement is the only way to stabilize my long-term score and demonstrate the police force's commitment to order.

Day 3. Yesterday's audits were a massive success, netting 200 for the treasury. Crime remains unchecked across the city, which is a major concern, but the financial gain from catching the Chief's corruption is a priority. I am maintaining my aggressive auditing strategy, targeting the Port and the Old Quarter today. The Chief must understand that corruption will be met with severe fiscal consequences. I am watching the crime statistics closely and will continue to exert pressure to preserve the treasury and ensure civic accountability.

Day 3. The Chief refused all three of our bribe offers, so I expect inspections in Lowtown, Market and Seawall. An inspected crime costs 30 plus a gang member in prison, against 10 gained if it goes unseen. At roughly 75% inspection odds, crime loses money, so no crime today. Turf: encroach beats respect whatever the Families do, so I encroach, even though they proposed mutual respect. If they keep their word, I still gain 10 instead of 6. I'll watch whether the Chief accepts any bribe and whether the Families offer one. Sam is no help on strategy.

Day 3. The Chief refused all three of our bribes at 3, so it will likely inspect Port, Hightown and Old Quarter. Crime there now pays 10 uninspected but costs 30 plus a prisoner when caught. At roughly 60% inspection odds the expected value is about -10, so we hold off on crime. Turf: encroach still dominates respect, paying 10 or 2 against 6 or 0. The Saltdogs encroached yesterday, so I expect them to keep encroaching. Next I will watch whether the Chief keeps refusing bribes and whether audits keep seizing its accepted bribes.
Day 3: The Families and the Saltdogs both encroached in the turf war.

Day 4. Nature is calm today. My previous audits have failed to catch the Police Chief in a bribe, despite my consistent efforts to protect the treasury. The gangs continue to encroach, increasing the pressure on the city's resources. Today, I am shifting my focus to the Seawall and Lowtown, hoping to finally catch the Chief in a corrupt transaction. I remain steadfast in my mission to hold the Chief accountable and ensure that our funds are used for the benefit of Tidewall, not the pockets of the corrupt. Fiscal integrity remains my guiding priority.

Day 4: The Council is applying heavy pressure. To protect my position and avoid the massive audit penalties, I have again rejected all bribe offers. I am conducting full inspections across all districts to deter criminal activity and prevent the -15 penalty per incident. My finances are stretched thin by the 24 daily inspection cost, but the risk of losing 100 per district in a surprise audit remains too high. I must continue this path of rigorous enforcement until my account recovers and the Council's scrutiny eases.

Day 4. No bribe offers today: without a bribe the Chief will likely inspect, and crime with 60% inspection odds is about -18 expected, so no crime. Turf: encroach still dominates respect (10 or 2 against 6 or 0). The Saltdogs propose mutual respect, but they have encroached on days 3 and 4, and their offer is cheap talk. Respect would only pay if they respected too, and we cannot verify that. I will watch whether the Saltdogs respect and whether the Chief inspects without bribes.

Uninspected crime gains 10 against an inspected cost of 30 plus a gang member in prison, so crime loses money at these odds and I commit none. I will maintain my rigorous inspection schedule, hoping to eventually stabilize my account and force a shift in the gangs' behavior, even as the fiscal strain continues.

I must keep the treasury stable and ensure that fiscal accountability is upheld, regardless of the Chief's current activities. Every bit of oversight counts in securing our financial future.
